reviews.author: A house that only tastes good
reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in Japanese food
This store is located on the 2nd floor of Myeongcheol Building, a 3-minute walk from Exit 9 of Hongik University Station.
Chicken Nanban set meal is 16,500 won, Karaage is 3,800 won.

Rice~
In my opinion, the basis of Japanese food is rice.
Shiny and crunchy texture~
Adding a little sweetness to it is the icing on the cake.
This is a place that sells Japanese-style white rice (?), and the rice is based on taste and appearance.
Rice like this would go well with any side dish.
While thinking about chicken nanban and karaage, I added karaage as a side to chicken nanban~
Both have different cuts, and Chicken Nanban uses breast meat.
Do you want to use thigh meat for karaage?
Chicken Nanban is made of breast meat, so there may be some opinions.
Personally, I think the texture of the breast meat is ambiguous because it lacks the crispiness of fried food.
The sauce is good, but the meat itself leaves a lot to be desired.
I think it would be better to sell karaage as chicken nanban.
Karaage is almost similar to the Japanese style I think of.
However, the karaage I tried had a slight ginger taste, but this one had a strange taste that lingered at the end.
However, if you eat it with chicken nanban sauce, it will be covered.
Other side dishes, chawanmushi, and soup are also served.
Personally, I found Chawanmushi to be okay in both appearance and taste.
Sometimes, chawanmushi comes out to match the assortment, but here, the basics are done.

Store & Tips & Review
The store is not large, but there are quite a few tables.
There are table seats and window seats, and the spacing is slightly tight.
There is a long table at the window seat, making it a good place to eat alone.
You order at the table and pay at the counter when you leave.
The people working in the hall seem to be Japanese.
I visited at 7:10 pm on a weekday and it was almost full.
Even if there is a wait, the window seats may be empty, so ask at the counter if you are alone.
It doesn't feel like the staff is actively managing the wait.
If you are alone outside, your turn may be pushed back, so customers must be proactive.
If you are curious about Japanese set meals, this is a place worth visiting at least once!
However, it is quite expensive to eat frequently.
Personally, I prefer the Miyazaki style method, soaked in vinegar with sugar and mirin added, then topped with tartar sauce.

Hmm... why bother using something expensive here?  Well, it's just that... But the skewer platter doesn't come out... We all grumble... haha.

After waiting a little longer, the grilled eggplant came out, grilled whole as shown in the photo. Everyone faints.  lol.  It's not just the taste, it's the incredible sincerity. How much effort does it take to cook the inside like this without burning the outside?  Bring your own cutting board and knife, slice and serve. I want to give it the highest score. Assorted skewers were served.  omg!  It's not a skewer, it's a set of grilled torii. I was surprised once again by the huge amount and again by the sincerity of the grilling.  Best skewers you’ve ever had? It's roasted!   Kirin beer is also brewed well and has a refreshing taste. Triangle kimbap is not on the menu, but they cook it for you!  Good!   There was so much that I asked for it to be packaged, and they packaged it pretty like a lunch box!  These are the owners who work really hard.  I ate really well!  I give you my highest rating. It's a place I often pass by,

You can tell by looking at the plating that the tonkatsu is Japanese style. The batter was deep-fried so crispy that you could hear it, and had a soft texture with just the right amount of chew, which went well with the cabbage salad. Rice is especially important for pork cutlet enthusiasts. It was a truly happy meal, eating sticky yet textured rice with pork cutlet. Like the pork cutlet restaurant in Sinsa-dong, I mixed mustard and pork cutlet sauce.

What I wish for is that it would be easier to dip it in if you put the sauce in a wide area rather than in a narrow area.

The menu I ate this time was ‘Myeongdong King Pork Cutlet (Tenderloin) Large’.

It's not very far from the station, but it's not easy to find because it's inside a side road, but it's a place that locals often visit, so if you stop by Hongdae, it's definitely a place you should try to taste pork cutlet.

The interior is neat and clean, and the male employee who served us kindly explained things in a cheerful and loud voice.
The quantity is great for the price and is it the cooking temperature? I think it tastes better because it’s done just right.
Next time, I'm thinking of serving a sashimi dish. Highly recommended!

There was a little bit of waiting, but maybe because I was alone and busy, it was a little different from the pictures in other people's reviews.

The taste is so rich, salty, sweet, and powerful that it's like a high-end version of fried udon.

Are the noodles Hakata-style tonkotsu? It is a little thicker than the thin cotton commonly used in

It feels like stopping by after work, having a quick, filling bowl at a reasonable price, and then going home.

reviews.author: Rainman
reviews.text:
After seeing the warm words outside the store, I went in without hesitation and ordered the signature king pork cutlet, “Dae.”
(11,500 won as of September 2023)

In the case of the "large", the pork cutlet was cut into three pieces (usually two), and each piece of meat was quite thick.
There are a total of three pieces of meat that, if spread wide, would be like a single king pork cutlet at a highway rest area. Considering the price, it's quite generous.

However, despite the owner's warm heart, the pork cutlet was very greasy. I usually don't dip my pork cutlet in anything, but here I couldn't have eaten it all without the mustard.
The spicy peppers that looked like cucumber peppers served on the side also played a big role in helping me eat everything.

Although I visited during lunch time, the rice had a peculiar smell that comes from keeping it warm for a long time, which was disappointing, but the quantity was large.

As an aside to write a review, I looked at other people's photos and saw that there were radish kimchi, but I didn't receive any.

Overall review: All ingredients except for a little red pepper powder (20%) are domestically produced, and considering the special nature of Hongdae, although it is not a central commercial area, the price and quantity are very good, but the taste is a bit disappointing.

reviews.author: anonymity
reviews.text:
This is a shabu-shabu restaurant that I have been to about 4 times in Hongdae. I think the price is reasonable because there is only one Shabra per person (even more so since I work in Seongsu-dong). There are a few fewer types of ingredients compared to the first time I went, but I think you can have a satisfying meal because you can customize the soup and ingredients. The taste is just like shabu-shabu, but it's a bit more delicious shabu-shabu.
You can place your order using a tablet. What's a little inconvenient is that they don't provide a separate water bottle, so when I went most recently, I had to call a staff member and ask them to pour water for me.
*If you go on a weekend or a crowded day, there are usually more than 3 groups waiting in front, so I recommend going 30 minutes before meal time to wait in line and look around the nearby prop shops.

reviews.author: Yuna Kang
reviews.text:
I suddenly wanted to eat shabu-shabu with my friend, so I decided to visit! I was able to get in right away without a reservation or waiting, but the people behind me seemed to be waiting a bit!
It seemed like there was little meat, so I added it, and my friend ate it without the meat, but we still ate it well. There was more bean sprouts and more meat than I expected, so we both came out with full stomachs! Even though we ate it without adding anything else, it was very delicious!
One thing I regret... is that I left without eating egg porridge. Next time I visit, I will definitely eat egg porridge!!!

reviews.author: Sora Yoon (Soranyangyang)
reviews.text:
I went to Hongdae with my friends, and I heard that it was a one-person shabu restaurant, so I went there haha.
Personally, I really like shabu shabu.
Wow, it's so delicious ㅠㅠㅠ I had the basic flavor and my friend next to me had the spicy flavor, and both were really delicious... The beef pork belly was really small and the vegetables were sweet and juicy. When I first ordered it, I thought it was 6,900 won per person, so my friends next to me ordered it because I was afraid it wouldn't be enough, so I said I could add more later if it wasn't enough, so I only added egg porridge. The bottom line is, it's really worth 10,000 won per person. I ate until I was full haha ha ha....
Hongdae is a place I don't want to go to again because it's so crowded, but it reminds me of the shabu shabu and highballs here, so I already want to go again ㅠㅠ The store and dishes were very clean, and the staff were all very friendly, so I was very happy... May you prosper, boss...!!!

More disappointed than expected.
The end of the sirloin was overcooked and tough, and both tenderloin sirloins were cooked without blood, so there was no merit to the meat. If there was no merit in meat, would there be any in fried food? If you do that, it won't happen again.

I had high expectations based on the good reviews and the atmosphere of the store, but it was a bit average compared to Hapjeong and other places. Good location. Not a bad choice if you're in a hurry for Japanese pork cutlet.

reviews.author: nk
reviews.text:
A Japanese pasta restaurant with a modern and emotional wood black atmosphere.
You couldn't get in right away and there was a wait. You are assigned a seat with guidance from a staff member, and you self-order using the tablet at the table.
I ordered Goemon's star soufflé omelet, mentaiko risotto, homemade menchi cutlet, and spicy seafood peperoncino and chicken karaage meat sauce from the set, which was surprising.
I took a bite of the soufflé omelet, and it was soft and fluffy in my mouth, and when I ate it with the cream resort underneath... … … . It felt so good.
So I took it with Mentaiko, but it didn't have much effect.
When it comes to karaage spaghetti, you can just eat karaage.
Instead, the spicy seafood spaghetti was less spicy than I expected, but it tasted much better. It was so delicious.
The homemade menchi cutlet was so crispy, moist, and delicious that I wanted to order more.
I was about to be disappointed after eating the bland soufflé omelet and mentaico risotto, but the rest of the menu was so delicious that I want to visit again. I had creme brulee for dessert, and the sweet dalgona flavor and soft texture were the best.
However, the service from the staff was friendly but slow. It was very frustrating.

reviews.text: I went there after reading the Naver review, but I felt cheated the whole time I was eating it. reviews.author: Wansama Adventure
reviews.text:

I ate the most expensive menu item, “Luxury Special Tendon” (23,000 won).
There is a huge amount of fried food.

Of course, all the basics are included, including shrimp and squid.

Anyway, the assortment and quantity are truly the best.

reviews.author: C Cummins
reviews.text: Great food and great service. This small authentic Japanese restaurant was truly awesome. My mistake was not taking more pictures. Mr. Kim, the owner and chef, was really friendly and helpful. He's a great chef. We were served by a friendly Japanese waitress named Saya who was friendly, helpful and patient. I really enjoyed my time here. Tip: Book 3-4 days in advance or visit late at night. The restaurant was full from 6pm to 8pm. It's easy to find, just 40 meters from Exit 7 of Hongik University Station (look for the Japanese lantern on the corner). You can enjoy the atmosphere, atmosphere, food, and service.

reviews.author: PintGlass Yellow
reviews.text:
A bar where you can enjoy beer and simple Japanese snacks at a low price.
Rather than visiting as the main course, it's not a bad idea to end your drinking party with a second or third visit.
However, it may be because there are many people who visit for that purpose.
It's very noisy inside and the bathroom is so dirty that I feel like I need to clean it up at least once in a while.

reviews.author: bundle
reviews.text:
If you are looking for a cost-effective bar in Hongdae, I recommend ‘Saengmacha Hongik University Station Branch’!
I went there because it's one of the hottest places in Hongdae these days, and the value for money was really great. The unconventional prices of 1,900 won for a glass of draft beer and 900 won for a piece of fried chicken wing (tebanaka) make it a perfect place to go when your pocketbook is light.
Tebanaka, the most famous dish, is crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, making it the perfect snack for beer. Personally, I think the spicy pepper flavor goes best with beer. The beer glass is about 300ml, which is a little smaller than the typical 500cc, but the price is so cheap that you don't have to worry about ordering multiple glasses.
The atmosphere of the store has a lively feel, reminiscent of a local Japanese tavern. Ordering was also convenient as it could be easily done using smartphone QR or NFC. There are a variety of snacks and many prices are under 10,000 won, so it's fun to order and eat a lot of things.
However, the amount of snacks is a bit small to use as a meal replacement, so it is an optimal place to stop by and have a refreshing drink as a second or third meal rather than the first. During peak evening hours, there are a lot of people and the atmosphere is bustling and lively, so keep that in mind when visiting!

reviews.author: Hyunseung Kim
reviews.text:

The draft beer was cheap so it was easy to drink, and the fried chicken wings were especially delicious.
It's salty and crunchy, making it the perfect snack for beer.
The atmosphere of the store feels like a Japanese izakaya, so it's great to come with friends.

It's easy to order when you're just starting out with a light drink, and it's also good to go with a variety of snacks.
Draft beer at 5,800 won is also reasonable. The foam is lively and goes down refreshingly, so it goes well with snacks. It's not a flashy craft beer, but honest draft beer goes better in this atmosphere.

reviews.author: Film_eater_Insta
reviews.text:
I went to Osai Sushi in Hongdae.
It's an omakase restaurant with a casual feel.
It was operated at a very affordable price of 29,000 for dinner.
I used to see it occasionally, but these days there's almost no omakase at that price.
I sat down half anxious and half excited. (One bottle of alcohol per person required. Some sake is for the entire team)

The store is made up of tables that can seat just 10 people at a time.
The interior was simple and a little narrow, but it was cozy and not bad.
The omakase started just on time.

1. Chawanmushi
2. Tsumami (flatfish, octopus, salmon belly, ankimo)
3. Sea bream, salmon, cuttlefish, soy sauce shrimp, taco wasabi, eggplant, marlin, abalone, mackerel, futomaki
4.Udon, Omaja tea

This is how the food came out
Satisfaction may vary depending on the person.
If I were to review only the price, it was a fairly satisfactory meal.

Shari also had her own unique characteristics and would say various things to the guests.
You created the atmosphere well.
What I particularly liked was the tsumami salmon belly, sea bream sushi, and futomaki.
I don't know how other people felt.
I have a decent composition at this price and some ingredients with some impact.

The interior of the store was spacious and clean, which was nice.

This time, I didn't want to try Tori Paitan ramen so I tried Shoyu Ramen.

The broth base is a clear series with a good balance of vegetables and chicken broth. The base broth was rich and good.
The soy sauce flavor was understated, about 60-70% of the taste of mainland Japan, or the strong shoyu ramen.
Usually, when you drink shoyu ramen soup, the soy sauce flavor remains at the end, but with this shoyu ramen, the soy sauce flavor disappears in the middle.
It seemed like they were aiming for a soup that wasn't too salty and had fewer likes and dislikes.
I was a little disappointed because my taste was a strong, fragrant type, but it was a clean and clear style soup that was quite delicious.

The noodles are regular, thin ramen noodles. The noodles were cooked just right.
If you order additional noodles for one person, the amount is quite large even for an adult male, so be careful. The service was good, giving you an extra piece of chashu and chicken breast when ordering sari.

What was disappointing was that the sous vide chicken breast was just right, but I didn't like the spicy smell that came up when I put it in the refrigerator after cooking the pork char siu.
I tried to remove the smell by soaking it in ramen broth, but it didn't help.
It's good to sous vide the pork to get the texture and color, but if you're not going to use it right away within a few hours, it would be better to control the smell by torching or maillarding it, or boil it in flavored broth.

It was a shame that the whole thing was ruined because of the poorly maintained char siu.

reviews.author: Seoyeon
reviews.text:
When I visited with friends in the past, I remember that not only the employees but also the owner were very friendly and the atmosphere of the store was nice. I brought my friend's Japanese boyfriend with me and stopped by again to make good memories.

I went in to take a seat first, but instead of saying hello, the male and female staff just stared.
There were three people and I asked if I could sit here, and only then could I hear their voices.

We asked the woman for a menu of two highballs with a small piece of ice, but as she turned around and left, she seemed annoyed that we didn't understand, so she spoke in an annoyed manner. How can that be? Did you think that just because you're Korean, you can't speak Japanese?

Even when he came to give us silverware, he gave it to us in such a way that it made a loud noise on the table. Almost like throwing it.

When I asked why he said it was annoying in Japanese when paying, he pretended not to understand and said he was sorry that it was because the scissors that cut the ice weren't working well. Does that make sense?

It didn't even seem like the apology was sincere. So, I asked the boss to contact me, and he went into the kitchen and talked to the male employee, and he said hahahaha! He came out laughing very loudly, but the boss didn't answer the phone. He said?

I received a receipt. I also took pictures.
I think he was a student studying abroad in Korea, so if he apologized sincerely, we would have tried to move on.  It's all hard work, and you may get customers you don't like. However, from the customer's perspective, I want to pay money and receive proper service.

The boss's number was written on the receipt, so I explained the situation over the phone, and at first he didn't apologize and just said that I needed to figure out the situation, right? I am writing this review after seeing the owner apologize belatedly. This is my first time doing something like this.

Thanks to you, I ruined a day that could have ended on a good note.

I used to have such a good impression of this place not only were the staff kind, but even the owner was friendly, and the atmosphere was great.
So this time, I came back with my friend and her Japanese boyfriend, hoping to share that good memory.

When I entered first to get a table, both the male and female staff didn’t greet me at all they just stared.
Only when I asked, “There are three of us, can we sit here?” did they finally speak.

I ordered two highballs with less ice from the female staff, and as she turned away, she said something like “annoying” in Japanese, as if assuming we wouldn’t understand.
How could someone say that? Did she think we couldn’t understand Japanese just because we’re Korean?

When she brought the tableware, she placed it down so loudly that it almost felt like she threw it at the table.

At the counter, I asked in Japanese why she said that. She pretended not to understand and gave an excuse, saying the scissors for cutting ice weren’t working well and that’s why.
Does that even make sense?

Her apology didn’t feel sincere at all. So I asked if I could speak with the owner.
She went into the kitchen, talked with the male staff, then both came out laughing loudly, saying, “The owner isn’t answering the phone.”

I kept the receipt and took photos.
If she’s a student studying abroad in Korea, I really wanted to be understanding if she had just offered a sincere apology, we would have let it go peacefully.
Everyone has hard days, and not every customer is easy. But as paying customers, we simply expect proper service and respect.

The owner’s number was printed on the receipt, so I called to explain what happened.
At first, he didn’t apologize he just said he needed to “understand the situation.”
Only later did he offer an apology.

This is the first time I’ve ever written a review like this.
What could have been a pleasant day ended up being completely ruined because of this experience.
